text:
You will suffer. You have already suffered.

Perhaps you are suffering.

And though you know

why (if you know it),

that knowledge will not be your consolation.


The farewell to your own; chance,

implacable; the unknown of

heaven,

everything that is lost

down deeds and life, down time,


or also up through life, toward what awaits you,

everything shapes the

flavor of your tears,

a flavor without flavor, since it is not shared


by the one who has seen you suffer

—he cannot share it—,

a flavor you do not

understand,

a heap of tears that traces,

I do not know where,

a

sea across which there drift,

and I do not know why,

useless forever,

inconsolable,

who knows since when,

his soul,

your soul

and

mine.

From

"" 1996

translation.title: A Sea of Tears
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps Marzal's address to suffering and the strange, unresolved bibliographic fragment at the end.
